default.notes: Apply for a B/2 visitor visa at an Israeli embassy or consulate before travel — expect to show proof of funds, ties to your home country and a return ticket; processing times vary by mission.

groups.notes: Visa-exempt for stays of up to 90 days, but an ETA-IL electronic travel authorisation (applied for online at israel-entry.piba.gov.il, valid 2 years) is now required before boarding.
Israeli law treats this country as an enemy state — its citizens are not admitted to Israel except with rare, individually granted permission from the Ministry of Interior.

There are no diplomatic relations with Israel — entry is possible only in exceptional cases with prior clearance and a visa arranged through the Israeli authorities; ordinary tourism is effectively not possible. Confirm any option with an Israeli mission in a third country.

IL.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Israeli citizens.

PS.notes: Holders of Palestinian Authority passports are subject to a separate permit regime administered through COGAT rather than the tourist visa system — entry to Israel generally requires an individual permit, and this applies even to Palestinian ID holders who also carry a foreign passport.
